questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the following sentence.**

I __need to put out__ my clothes before I leave for work this morning otherwise, I will be restless when I return.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'need to put away'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined part in the given sentence is** grammatically incorrect.**
 
• Here, **'need to put away'** should be used instead of** 'need to put out'.**
 
• **"Put out" **typically means *to extinguish something or to place something outside*, while **"put away" **means *to store or place something in its proper location.*
 
• Here's why **"put away"** is more fitting in this context:
 
 
• *"I need to put away my clothes before I leave for work this morning otherwise, I will be restless when I return."*
 
• This implies that the clothes will be properly** stored or placed in their designated locations**, like in a closet or dresser. When using *"put away,"* it indicates a sense of organization and tidiness, ensuring that the clothes are stored properly and not left out.
 
 
 
• So, if the intention is to ensure the clothes are neatly stored or arranged in their proper place before leaving for work to avoid feeling restless upon return,** "put away"** would be more suitable than **"put out."** 

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *I **need to put away** my clothes before I leave for work this morning otherwise, I will be restless when I return.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The novel highlights the __place__ of the endangered species in the rainforest.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"place"** in this context means a particular position or point in space. (स्थान)

 
 
• **Example:** The **place** where the concert was held was packed with people.
 
 
 
• **"Plight"** refers to a dangerous, difficult, or otherwise unfortunate situation. (दुर्दशा)
 
 
• **Example:** The** plight **of the homeless is a serious issue that needs attention.
 
 

Hence, we can infer that the word** 'plight'** is more appropriate in **the context of endangered species, as it highlights their dangerous and unfortunate situation.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Perspective** (दृष्टिकोण): A particular attitude toward or way of regarding something; a point of view.

 
 
• **Example:** Her** perspective** on the issue was quite different from mine.
 
 
 
• **Position** (स्थिति): A place where someone or something is located or has been put.
 
 
• **Example:** The** position** of the statue in the park is quite prominent.
 
 
 
• **Prowess** (कौशल): Skill or expertise in a particular activity or field.
 
 
• **Example:** His** prowess** in mathematics is well-known among his peers.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Bill Gates’ fortune was bequeathed __for the old age home__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"bequeath"** means to leave (a personal estate or one's body) to a person or other beneficiary by a will. (वसीयत में देना)

 
 
• **Example:** He **bequeathed** his entire estate to his daughter.
 
 
 
• **"To"** is used to indicate the recipient of something. (को)
 
 
• **Example:** She gave the book** to** her friend.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct preposition to use in this context is **"to"**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Into the old age home** (पुराने उम्र के घर में): This phrase suggests movement or direction towards the inside of something.

 
 
• **Example:** She walked** into the old age home **to visit her grandmother.
 
 
 
• **With the old age home** (पुराने उम्र के घर के साथ): This phrase suggests association or accompaniment.
 
 
• **Example:** He worked **with the old age home** to improve their facilities.
 
 
 
• **By the old age home** (पुराने उम्र के घर द्वारा): This phrase indicates the agent performing the action.
 
 
• **Example:** The event was organized **by the old age home.**

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the following sentence.

I consider that every matter must be considered __in every point__ of view
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"considered in every point of view"** means to examine or think about something from all possible angles or perspectives. (हर दृष्टिकोण से विचार करना)

 
 
• **Example: **In order to make a fair decision, the judge **considered the case in every point of view.**
 
 
 
• **"from every point"** indicates examining something from every perspective or angle. (हर दृष्टिकोण से)
 
 
• **Example: **We need to analyze the project** from every point** before moving forward.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the correct phrase to use in the given context is **'from every point'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: '**Option 2.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **on every point** (हर बिंदु पर): This phrase is not commonly used and does not fit well in the given context.

 
 
• **Example:** He insisted on every point without considering the overall picture.
 
 
 
• **of every point** (हर बिंदु का): This phrase is also not commonly used and is not appropriate in the given context.
 
 
• **Example:** The analysis of every point was thorough, but it missed the broader perspective.
 
 
 
• **at every point** (हर बिंदु पर): This phrase is incorrect for the given context as it implies specific locations rather than perspectives.
 
 
• **Example:** Security checks were conducted at every point along the route.
